touches.text: Seals: one current validation per proof, beside the proof. A seal holds while the code it measured is unchanged.
A timed-out run is its own outcome, not red.
Notices: what a run saw that nobody asked about, surfaced to the operator.
Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).

Commit: the proofs of the component the ticket changed, since RULE 1 bounds a change to its component. Passing them puts the component in service, yellow: proven where it changed, not yet measured against what depends on it. Akien: "being put in service only requires that it's the best we can do now. only requires 80% trust."

Hourly: an entry on Cairn's scheduled list (5.9) reseals every yellow component and everything that depends on it. Commit a is fine and commit b is fine, and an hour later the run finds a new red. That is the system doing what it was designed to do (Akien 2026-11-13), and the window to search is one hour's landings. Hourly confirmed by Akien 2026-11-13: "perfect. yes that."

Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Akien 2026-11-13: "every test failure, every orphaned file, HAS TO BE FIXED. if we get 3 reds but they're really not related to what we just did, we can ticket them for fixing. reds don't get lost." and "so each run writes any new bugs". Once a red unrelated to a crossing is ticketed, that crossing can go ahead.
VERBS: run, notices, CodeMother's verbs reached over the bus (RULE 1). COMMANDS: cairn codemother test (--hollow, --seal, --exec, ...), shortcut cairn test; proofgate (the hook: proofs run by hand).

[Q#101: proofgate reads the text of a Bash command, so a proof run from a script file ("bash run_it.sh", whose text names no proof) is invisible to it. Measured 2026-11-13: such a proof runs bare and writes into the live HOME/.cairn. Which should seal that spelling? (a) every proof refuses to run unless it is inside the tester's seal, as one check in a shared helper or at the scratch door; (b) the hook also reads the script file a bash/sh command names; (c) a proof run from a script file is accepted as outside the rule. CC leans (a): it is the only one that covers every spelling, not just the next one found. This reopens ticket 72a37498c601's WRONG INTENT clause; ticket dda0e72b9c67 clause 4 waits on it (open-49fc67a40ede).]

Once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus: the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py, the other code sites and the 82 proofs that run a sieve over themselves. No published client tool, no fifth exception. Akien 2026-11-13, on Q#88: "over the bus. that's what it's for?"

The verdict's instrument run is a seal-grade run, so it runs where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), under bubblewrap. A box without bubblewrap (Windows) asks for it and does not run it itself. A bwrap-only tooth reads not-run on such a box, never red; its outcome is the sealer's. CC's decision, 2026-11-13, on Q#98, following Akien's answer to Q#90.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
